title: Lanthanides (4f Series): Configurations, +3 Dominance, & Contraction
topics: Lanthanide Electronic Configuration: [Xe] 4f^(1-14) 5d^(0-1) 6s² (Ce Z=58 to Lu Z=71)
Dominant Oxidation State (+3) & Anomalous Stability (+2 in Eu²⁺, Yb²⁺; +4 in Ce⁴⁺, Tb⁴⁺)
Lanthanide Contraction Mechanism (Poor 4f Shielding: s > p > d > f)
Consequences: 4d/5d Radii Similarity (Zr ≈ Hf = 1.59 Å), Difficult Separation by Ion-Exchange, Basicity Trend of Hydroxides (La(OH)₃ > ... > Lu(OH)₃)
Mischmetall Alloy (95% Ln metals, Ce 50%, 5% Fe)
quickSummary: Lanthanides fill the 4f subshell ([Xe] 4f^(1-14) 5d^(0-1) 6s²). Dominant OS is +3; Ce⁴⁺ (4f⁰) and Tb⁴⁺ (4f⁷) are strong oxidants; Eu²⁺ (4f⁷) and Yb²⁺ (4f¹⁴) are strong reducers. Lanthanide Contraction results from poor 4f shielding, causing Zr ≈ Hf (1.59 Å) and basicity decrease La(OH)₃ > ... > Lu(OH)₃.
summary: Master lanthanide configurations, +3 dominance, redox behavior of anomalous states, lanthanide contraction, and hydroxide basicity.

conceptBreakdown.title: 7. Lanthanides Overview & Oxidation States

summaryBox.title: Lanthanide Configurations & States
summaryBox.takeaway: +3 is universal. Ce⁴⁺ (4f⁰) and Tb⁴⁺ (4f⁷) are oxidizing agents; Eu²⁺ (4f⁷) and Yb²⁺ (4f¹⁴) are reducing agents.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
LANTHANIDE CONFIGURATION
                           
   $$\mathbf{[\text{Xe}] \, 4f^{1-14} \, 5d^{0-1} \, 6s^2}$$
   
   ├── $\text{La} (Z=57): [\text{Xe}] 5d^1 6s^2$      ├── $\text{Eu} (Z=63): [\text{Xe}] 4f^7 6s^2$ (Half-filled $4f^7$)
   ├── $\text{Ce} (Z=58): [\text{Xe}] 4f^1 5d^1 6s^2$  ├── $\text{Yb} (Z=70): [\text{Xe}] 4f^{14} 6s^2$ (Fully-filled $4f^{14}$)
   └── $\text{Gd} (Z=64): [\text{Xe}] 4f^7 5d^1 6s^2$  └── $\text{Lu} (Z=71): [\text{Xe}] 4f^{14} 5d^1 6s^2$

                      ANOMALOUS LANTHANIDE OXIDATION STATES
                      
   $\mathbf{\text{Ce}^{4+} (4f^0):}$   Noble gas core; strong **Oxidizing Agent** in aqueous solution ($\text{Ce}^{4+} \rightarrow \text{Ce}^{3+}$).
   $\mathbf{\text{Eu}^{2+} (4f^7):}$   Half-filled stability; strong **Reducing Agent** ($\text{Eu}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{Eu}^{3+}$).
   $\mathbf{\text{Yb}^{2+} (4f^{14}):}$ Fully-filled stability; strong **Reducing Agent** ($\text{Yb}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{Yb}^{3+}$).
   $\mathbf{\text{Tb}^{4+} (4f^7):}$   Half-filled stability; strong **Oxidizing Agent** ($\text{Tb}^{4+} \rightarrow \text{Tb}^{3+}$).
conceptBreakdown.content:
The Lanthanides (Inner Transition Elements) comprise the 14 elements from Cerium ($\text{Ce}, Z=58$) to Lutetium ($\text{Lu}, Z=71$), where 4f subshells are filled.
- **Dominant OS**: $+3$ is the universal, most stable state ($\text{Ln}^{3+}$).
- **Anomalous States**: Attained by gaining $4f^0$, $4f^7$, or $4f^{14}$.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 7.2 Lanthanide Contraction & Its Consequences
conceptBreakdown.title: 7.2 Lanthanide Contraction & Its Consequences
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
LANTHANIDE CONTRACTION CURVE
                      
   Ionic Radius ($\text{Ln}^{3+}$) ▲
                                 │ \
                                 │  \   Steady, smooth decrease from
                                 │   \  $\text{La}^{3+} (1.06\text{ \AA})$ to $\text{Lu}^{3+} (0.86\text{ \AA})$
                                 0 └───┴──────────────────────────► Atomic Number ($Z$)

Major Consequences of Lanthanide Contraction:
1. 4d and 5d Series Radii Similarity: r(Zr_4d) ≈ r(Hf_5d) = 1.59 Å.
2. Difficult Separation: Identical chemical properties require Ion-Exchange Chromatography.
3. Basicity Trend: La(OH)₃ is MOST basic; Lu(OH)₃ is LEAST basic.
   Basicity Order: La(OH)₃ > Ce(OH)₃ > ... > Lu(OH)₃
conceptBreakdown.content:
Across the 14 lanthanides, nuclear charge increases by +1 per element into inner 4f orbitals. Because 4f orbitals are diffuse, they exhibit extremely poor electrostatic shielding ($\mathbf{\text{Shielding: } s > p > d > f}$).
- **Consequences**:
  1. **$4d$ and $5d$ Radii Similarity**: $r(\text{Zr}_{4d}) \approx r(\text{Hf}_{5d}) = 1.59\text{ \AA}$.
  2. **Difficult Separation**: Separated using Ion-Exchange Chromatography.
  3. **Basicity of Hydroxides**: $\mathbf{\text{La(OH)}_3 > \text{Ce(OH)}_3 > \dots > \text{Lu(OH)}_3}$.

quickRevision: +3 is the most stable state for all lanthanides.
Ce⁴⁺ (4f⁰) is a strong oxidizing agent; Eu²⁺ (4f⁷) is a strong reducing agent.
Lanthanide Contraction causes r(Zr) ≈ r(Hf) = 1.59 Å.
Hydroxide basicity: La(OH)₃ (most basic) > ... > Lu(OH)₃ (least basic).
